description: The LP domain commands ClientOps uses, as GET http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/protocol describes them.
trimmed: commands keeps getSemanticTree, getInteractiveElements, getNodeDetails, detectForms, clickNode, fillNode, waitForSelector, waitUntil (18 in the LP domain)

commands.name: getSemanticTree
commands.description: The main frame's DOM as an accessibility-style tree: each node's role, name, value and state, without scripts, styles, SVG and hidden content. Errors with InvalidNodeId when backendNodeId is unknown.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: text returns an indented plain-text outline instead of a JSON tree. It is more compact.

parameters.name: prune
parameters.description: Drop wrapper elements with no label and no interactivity, and text already contained in its parent's name. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: interactiveOnly
parameters.description: Keep only interactive elements and named content such as headings, list items, cells and landmarks. Takes precedence over prune. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: backendNodeId
parameters.description: Root the tree at this node instead of the document.

parameters.name: maxDepth
parameters.description: Stop walking below this many levels from the root.

returns.name: semanticTree
returns.description: The text outline when format is text. Otherwise the root node as an object with nodeId, backendDOMNodeId, nodeName, xpath, nodeType and children. Elements also have role and isInteractive, and when they apply: name, value, attributes, isDisabled, checked, ariaExpanded, ariaChecked and options (value, text, selected) for select lists. Text nodes have nodeValue.

commands.name: getInteractiveElements
commands.description: Lists the visible elements a user can act on, in document order: links, buttons, form controls, elements with an interactive ARIA role, contenteditable elements, elements with event listeners and elements with an explicit tabindex. Elements with pointer-events: none are left out. Errors with InvalidNodeId when nodeId is unknown.

parameters.name: nodeId
parameters.description: Backend node id. Only list elements inside this node instead of the whole main frame.

returns.name: elements
returns.description: One object per element, with backendNodeId, tagName, role, name (null when there is none), type (why it counts as interactive: native, aria, contenteditable, listener or focusable) and tabIndex. When they apply: listeners (the event types listened to), disabled, overlay (fixed and dialog, when the element sits in a position: fixed box or in an open dialog or popover), id, class, href (resolved to an absolute URL), inputType, value, elementName (the name attribute) and placeholder.

commands.name: getNodeDetails
commands.description: Details on one node: its role and name, whether it is interactive, its current value, and a CSS selector that finds it. Errors with InvalidNodeId when backendNodeId is unknown.

returns.name: nodeDetails
returns.description: An object with backendNodeId, tagName (text for a text node), role and isInteractive. When they apply: name, isDisabled, value (a non-empty password shows as *****; for an iframe, its current URL), inputType, placeholder, href (resolved to an absolute URL), id, class, selector, checked (checkboxes and radios) and options (value, text and selected) for a select or an input with a datalist. selector is the simplest CSS selector for which querySelector returns this element.

commands.name: detectForms
commands.description: Lists the main frame's <form> elements and the fields a user can fill in. A field outside the <form> that points to it with the form attribute is included. Hidden inputs and buttons (submit, button, image inputs and <button>) are left out, and so is a form with no fields left.

returns.name: forms
returns.description: One object per form, in document order, with backendNodeId, method (get, post or dialog, lowercase; get when the attribute is missing or not valid), fields, and action (the raw attribute, when not empty). Each field has backendNodeId, tagName (input, textarea or select), required and disabled. When they apply: name, inputType (input only), value (a non-empty password shows as *****), placeholder and options (value and text of each <option> in a select).

commands.name: clickNode
commands.description: Clicks an element the way a user does: the pointer moves over it, then the pointer and mouse down, up and click events fire as trusted events, focus moves as on a real mousedown, and the click's default action runs, such as following a link, submitting a form or toggling a checkbox. A disabled control gets the pointer events only. Returns once the events are dispatched, without waiting for a navigation the click starts. Errors with InvalidNodeId when the node is unknown, and InvalidParam when no id is given or the node is not an element.

parameters.name: nodeId
parameters.description: Same as backendNodeId, which it overrides when both are given.

commands.name: fillNode
commands.description: Replaces the value of an <input>, <textarea> or <select> the way a user does. The element takes focus first. In a text control (text, email, number, <textarea>, and the like), the current text is selected and the new text typed over it: beforeinput, textInput and input fire as trusted events, then change. A control without a text cursor (date, color, range, and the like) takes the value whole, then input and change fire. A <select> picks the first option whose value is text, or none when no option matches, then input and change fire. Errors with InvalidNodeId when the node is unknown, with InvalidParam when no id is given or the element is not one of these, is a checkbox or radio, or is a disabled or read-only input or textarea, and with InternalError when a page script cancels the edit.

parameters.name: nodeId
parameters.description: Same as backendNodeId, which it overrides when both are given.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The new value. For a <select>, the value of the option to pick.

commands.name: waitForSelector
commands.description: Waits until an element matching the CSS selector is in the main frame's document, then returns the first match. It waits for the document to be parsed first, then checks again as the page runs scripts and loads. The element only has to exist: it can still be hidden. If a navigation is in progress, it waits on the new document. Errors with InvalidParam when the selector is not valid or only targets pseudo-elements, and with InternalError when timeout runs out first.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: A CSS selector, as for querySelector.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Milliseconds. Defaults to 5000 when the page has finished loading, and 15000 while it is still loading.

returns.name: backendNodeId
returns.description: The first matching element, for use with getNodeDetails, clickNode or fillNode.

commands.name: waitUntil
commands.description: Blocks until the main frame reaches the condition, the --wait-until values. settled is load, then the requests and short timers that page-load work started, ignoring intervals, long timeouts, idle callbacks and WebSocket traffic; it is also announced as a Page.lifecycleEvent named settled. Drivers map their own waitUntil onto a fixed list of lifecycle names, so settled is awaited through this method. Errors with Timeout when timeout runs out first.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Milliseconds. Defaults to the page wait timeout.
